name: Dafy V-Integra Renal Met homemade diet balancer
note: Phosphorus-free vitamin-mineral balancer for home-made diets needing phosphorus restriction (dogs and cats), the V-Integra Renal formula with added DL-methionine (58,200 mg/kg) - for recipes low in methionine, e.g. plant-based. Free from animal-derived ingredients (manufacturer); vitamin D3 source not stated. Label: Ca 14.8%, P 0%, Na 1.3%, K 7.5%, Mg 1.1%, protein 10.2%, fat 2.5%, ash 61.5% (HCl-insoluble 4.2%), moisture 2.8%, lysine 0.1%, methionine 5.8%. Crude protein is almost all non-protein nitrogen (added methionine, taurine, choline) - no protein ingredients, so other amino acids are ~0 but left blank as on the label. Composition: calcium carbonate, potassium carbonate, maize starch, maltodextrin, magnesium carbonate, vegetable oils and fats, sodium chloride, sodium bicarbonate. Per kg: vit A 245,000 IU, D3 24,500 IU, B1 117 mg, B2 245 mg, B6 48 mg, B12 1.50 mg, C 1,220 mg, K3 10 mg, niacin 490 mg, Ca pantothenate 440 mg, folic acid 9.6 mg, biotin 2.5 mg, choline chloride 49,000 mg (= ~36,600 mg choline), taurine 39,200 mg, DL-methionine 58,200 mg, Fe 2,500 mg, Cu 245 mg, Mn 98 mg, Zn 4,400 mg, I 44 mg, Se 5.3 mg. No vitamin E declared (tocopherols only as antioxidant). Methionine acidifies urine and adds to the acid load. Calcium is mostly carbonate - given with the meal it also binds some phosphorus (not counted here). Label dose: dog 6-10 kg 5-8 g/day (1-5 kg 2-4 g); scoop = 5 g; add just before feeding, do not reheat; build up over 3 weeks (1/3, 2/3, full). Not for use with complete commercial foods unless planned by a nutritionist. Energy estimated. Source: dafynutrition.com/products/v-integra-renal-met.
